1. Accused in S.C.No.80/2023 pending before the Court of the Principal District and Sessions Judge,
Gadag arising out of Crime No.40/2023 registered by Mulugund police station, Gadag for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 504 of IPC, is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: 3. FIR in Crime No.40/2023 was registered by Mulugund police station, Gadag against the petitioner herein initially for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 307, 323 of IPC on the complaint of Salim who is the brother of the victim Reshma Husain Shekh.
In the said case, the petitioner was arrested on 30.05.2023.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Bail application filed by the petitioner NC: 2024:KHC-D:3621 before the trial Court in Crl.Misc.361/2023 was rejected on 06.10.2023.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that the version of alleged eyewitness CW6 in her statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. and under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. are inconsistent.
The petitioner has no criminal antecedents and he has two minor children who are required to be taken care of.
He is in custody from 30.05.2023 onwards.

Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the bail application.
6. FIR in Crime No.40/2023 was registered by Mulugund police station, Gadag on the complaint of Salim which was lodged on 30.05.2023, at about 9.05 a.m.

In the complaint, it is averred that the complainant's sister was married to the petitioner herein about 12 years prior to the date of the complaint and from the wedlock, the couple have two children.

It is further averred that the NC:
2024:KHC-D:3621 petitioner was ill-treating his wife and therefore the complainant had brought back his sister-Reshma along with the two minor children to his house about 15 days prior to the Hussain S/O Dastageersab Shekh vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94961448/
2 date of the complaint.
7.

sentences.text: On 29.05.2023, the petitioner allegedly came to the house of the complainant and requested him to send his wife with him as he intended to visit Davalmalik Hillock at Mulugund.
The complainant allegedly sent his cousin sister-Simran along with the petitioner and Reshma.

At about 6.30 p.m. on the said date, Simran allegedly telephoned the complainant and informed him that the petitioner had pushed down Reshma from the Hillock and she has sustained grievous injury and therefore she was taken to the hospital.
Immediately the complainant went to the hospital and noticed that Reshma had suffered grievous injury and she was not in a position to talk.

It is in this background,
on 30.05.2023 a complaint was lodged based on which FIR in Crime No.40/2023 was registered.
Reshma had subsequently died in the hospital on NC: 2024:KHC-D:3621 31.05.2023.
Therefore Section 302 of IPC was invoked against the accused.
8. According to the prosecution, CW6-Simran was the eyewitness to the incident in question.

In the complaint, it is averred that Simran had informed the complainant at about 6.30 p.m. on 29.05.2023 that petitioner had pushed down Reshma from the Hillock and as a result of the fall,
Reshma had suffered grievous injury and she was taken to the hospital and immediately thereafter complainant visited the hospital.
The complaint was lodged belatedly i.e., on the next date at about 9.05 a.m.

The statement made by the eyewitness CW6 before the police under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.
and the statement made by her before the jurisdictional Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. are inconsistent.
From a perusal of the statement of CWs.7 and 8 who are the other alleged eyewitnesses, a serious doubt arises as to whether they had witnessed the petitioner pushing down his wife from the hillock.
The petitioner, who was arrested on 30.05.2023, has no criminal antecedents.
Investigation in NC: 2024:KHC-D:3621 the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
He is required to take care of his two minor children.
Under these circumstances, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail is required to be answered in the affirmative.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail in S.C.No.80/2023 pending before the Court of the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Gadag arising out of Crime No.40/2023 registered by Mulugund police station, Gadag for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 504 of IPC,
subject to the following conditions:
i.

ii.
